title: canon-ignore-guard.sh reads its rules from the worktree and its attribution from the index, so a staged ignore rule reaching intent/.canon/ can pass
body:
Raised upstream on hv's ruling of 2026-09-14 (relayed by laksa-vc), filed by vc at 2026-09-14 17:03Z.

`lib/templates/hooks/canon-ignore-guard.sh` reads its RULES from the worktree and its ATTRIBUTION from the index. `git check-ignore -v --no-index` consults the worktree's `.gitignore`; `added_pairs` comes from `git diff --cached`. Measured by Laksa's dc (2026-09-12) with a `.gitignore` carrying `intent/.canon/` staged in a throwaway index: the guard's own diff reports `+intent/.canon/` at line 131 and `check-ignore` reports no match at all. The `source:lineno` comparison then compares line numbers across two different documents whenever index and worktree differ, which on a shared tree is routine (`git commit --only` plus a re-staging formatter is the house pattern). So a staged rule that would un-commit the canon estate can pass the guard.

Fix: split the guard so both halves read one document, the staged `.gitignore`: write the index blob out and run `check-ignore` against it (a temporary work tree, or the blob as the one rules file), and attribute added lines against that same blob. Laksa's arm for this guard (dc) is held on the split; the harness shape there (a temp-repo fixture versus driving the body) follows the fix. Lane: dc.


CLOSED 2026-09-14 (dc): both halves of `lib/templates/hooks/canon-ignore-guard.sh` now read one document, the staged one. Every ignore file the index holds is checked out into a scratch work tree (`git checkout-index --prefix`), and `git check-ignore -v --no-index` runs against that tree. The rules and the line numbers they are attributed by are therefore the commit's. If the scratch tree cannot be built, the guard refuses and does not check nothing.

New harness: `tests/unit/canon_ignore_guard.bats`. Its first two cases are the divergence in both directions:
- a rule reaching canon that is staged but not in the worktree must BLOCK, and names `.gitignore:2`;
- a worktree-only rule at the line number the commit adds must PASS.
The other cases cover an added `intent/.*/`, a nested `intent/.gitignore`, a future-path-only rule, a harmless rule, an inherited rule (reported, never failed on), and a commit touching no ignore file.

Judged in dc's worktree (scratchpad batch/judge-0392.txt):
- Against the guard before the fix, exactly the two divergence cases fail.
- With the fix, all 8 pass. shellcheck is clean, the syntax checks under /bin/bash 3.2, and `guard_dispatch.bats` and `templates_bash32.bats` pass.
